Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: When x is divided by eight, the remainder is four. Yuval claims: two x is necessarily divisible by eight. Noga claims: x is necessarily divisible by four. Itay claims: x is necessarily divisible by twelve. Which of the following is correct?
So we know the remainder by eight, and three claims about other divisors. [short pause] We'll solve it three ways, by understanding, with algebra, and then plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Let's start with understanding. x is full eights plus a remainder of four. When the new divisor divides eight, the full eights divide by it too, so only the remainder matters.
Yuval, two x by eight. The same eight, so only the remainder counts, doubled. Two times four is eight, and eight divides by eight. Yuval is right.
Noga, x by four. Four divides eight, so only the remainder matters. Four over four, no remainder. Noga is right.

Itay, x by twelve. Twelve doesn't divide eight, so from a remainder by eight we can't know the remainder by twelve. For example, x is four. Four divided by eight leaves four, and four doesn't divide by twelve. Itay is wrong.
So only Itay is wrong, choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is algebra. What's different? Instead of thinking about the remainder, we write x as an expression and take out a common factor. x is full eights plus four, so x is eight k plus four.
Yuval. Two x is sixteen k plus eight. Take out the eight, and it's eight times, in brackets, two k plus one. So it divides by eight. Yuval is right.
Noga. Take out a four from x, and it's four times, in brackets, two k plus one. So it divides by four. Noga is right.

Itay. x is four times two k plus one. For twelve, we'd need a three inside two k plus one, and it isn't always there. With k zero, two k plus one is one, and x is four, not divisible by twelve. Itay is wrong. Choice number two.
at: Itay is wrong. Choice number two

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in numbers that leave four when divided by eight, four and twelve.
Two x is eight or twenty-four, both divide by eight. Four and twelve both divide by four. But four doesn't divide by twelve, so Itay is wrong.

Careful, examples that work don't prove Yuval and Noga right, the first two ways do. But one example that fails proves Itay wrong. So choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
